reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 discusses a different alloy system (W-Ta-Cr-V) and notes V-rich precipitates as detrimental, which conflicts with the premise of improved ductility. E2 describes irradiation hardening in Hf1Ta HEA and mentions lattice distortion reducing defect size, but this is a general HEA concept not specifically linked to vanadium in NbMoTaW, and it does not address room-temperature ductility or high-temperature strength retention.
premises: Vanadium addition introduces localized lattice distortions and strain fields in BCC NbMoTaW.
These lattice distortions promote dislocation nucleation and movement at room temperature, improving ductility.
Lattice distortions act as defect recombination centers during irradiation, reducing helium bubble nucleation and growth.
A high-temperature homogenization anneal at ~1600 °C maintains overall BCC structural stability.
The modified alloy retains high strength and BCC stability at 1600 °C.
